title: Immutable Dependency Closures
summary: A runtime generation atomically snapshots its declared dependencies and holds them alive for its own lifetime.
why: Ensures that if Component A depends on Component B (v1), it continues to see B (v1) even if B (v2) is activated globally.
invariants: A live/warm generation keeps every generation in its declared dependency closure alive until the owning generation is released.
Dependency sets are captured through one atomic multi-module snapshot.
A replacement generation must be staged to bind a newer dependency version.
